lessons.title: Planning Academic Travel
lessons.objective: Learners will understand and correctly use make arrangements for and provide evidence of in academic contexts.

reading.text: The department will make arrangements for students to attend a regional conference. Each applicant must provide evidence of how the event relates to their research. Because the travel fund is limited, the panel will compare the purpose and expected benefit of each visit. Students should describe a specific session they plan to attend rather than simply listing the speakers they admire.

sentences.text: The department will make arrangements for students to attend a regional conference.
Each applicant must provide evidence of how the event relates to their research.
Because the travel fund is limited, the panel will compare the purpose and expected benefit of each visit.
Students should describe a specific session they plan to attend rather than simply listing the speakers they admire.

targets.meaningEn: to plan and organize something so it can happen
targets.meaningVi: sắp xếp, tổ chức cho việc gì

targets.meaningEn: to supply proof or details showing that something is true or relevant
targets.meaningVi: cung cấp bằng chứng về việc gì

exercises.prompt: In 'The department will make arrangements for students to attend a regional conference,' what does 'make arrangements for' mean here?

options.text: The department will plan and organize the necessary details so students can attend.
options.explanation: Correct because it captures planning and organizing to make attendance possible.

options.text: The department will cancel the conference, so students cannot attend.
options.explanation: Wrong because cancellation prevents attendance instead of arranging for it.

options.text: The department will ask students which speakers they admire, without planning their attendance.
options.explanation: Wrong because collecting opinions about speakers is different from organizing attendance.

exercises.explanation: The department is planning and organizing what is needed so students can attend.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'make arrangements for' naturally and correctly.

options.text: The office made arrangements for visitors to park in the nearby garage during the event.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the fixed collocation for plus the to-infinitive correctly.

options.text: The office made arrangements of visitors to park in the nearby garage during the event.
options.explanation: Wrong because the fixed collocation requires for, so change of to for.

options.text: The office made arrangements for visitors park in the nearby garage during the event.
options.explanation: Wrong because the verb needs to, so change park to to park.

exercises.explanation: Only one option keeps for plus the to-infinitive correctly.

exercises.prompt: In 'Each applicant must provide evidence of how the event relates to their research,' what does 'provide evidence of' mean here?

options.text: Each applicant must supply details or proof showing the connection to their research.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches supplying proof showing relevance.

options.text: Each applicant must promise to attend every session at the event.
options.explanation: Wrong because promising attendance does not mean supplying proof of relevance.

options.text: Each applicant must pay a fee to confirm their interest in the event.
options.explanation: Wrong because paying a fee does not mean supplying proof of relevance.

exercises.explanation: Applicants must supply proof showing how the event relates to research.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'provide evidence of' naturally and correctly.

options.text: The team provided evidence of improved safety after the new training program.
options.explanation: Correct because improved safety is a noun phrase that can follow of.

options.text: The team provided evidence of that safety improved after the new training program.
options.explanation: Wrong because of cannot introduce a finite that-clause here; write evidence that safety improved or evidence of improved safety.

options.text: The team provided evidence of improve safety after the new training program.
options.explanation: Wrong because the base verb improve cannot serve as the noun-phrase complement after of; use improved safety.

exercises.explanation: Only a uses evidence of with a noun phrase: improved safety. In b, of is incorrectly followed by a finite clause; in c, the base verb improve does not form the complement after of.

exercises.prompt: You are planning a weekend trip with friends. Write 2-3 sentences to a friend explaining what you have organized for accommodation and transport. Use make arrangements for or a natural inflection of it.
exercises.sampleAnswer: I have made arrangements for our stay at a guesthouse near the beach. I also booked a minibus so we can travel together on Saturday morning.
selfCheck: I wrote 2-3 sentences about a weekend trip with friends, not a conference application.
I used made arrangements for or another natural form of the phrase correctly.
My sentences are clear, natural, and describe accommodation and transport.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.

findings.message: On the initial hash, q4 treated evidences as always wrong. Oxford notes evidences is sometimes used in academic English. Replaced it with an objectively invalid of + finite-clause construction and a bare-verb complement error; both final reviewers confirm the corrected q4 has one defensible answer.

On the initial hash, q1 added unsupported travel/registration/support details. Rewrote options and explanations to focus only on planning attendance, cancellation, and speaker preferences; both final reviewers confirm the revised wording.
